lessons.pregame_expectation: 2 published claims said the same thing: EdgeDesk prices this game at Tennessee +7.0 with a fair total of 55.0, which makes Alabama the better team here by that margin on this field. EdgeDesk makes it Tennessee +7.0 where the market has Tennessee +5.5 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at FanDuel — a 1.3 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Alabama Crimson Tide lost by 16 where EdgeDesk projected a 6.8-point edge. Alabama Crimson Tide lost by 16.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Alabama as better in market and the game went the other way, across 2 separate published claims. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: Tennessee Volunteers won the game outright
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 8.1 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: Alabama holds the largest measured edge in this matchup: Alabama 60.5 (#28 of 138) vs Tennessee 54.6 (#113 of 138) — 85 places on the national board.
lessons.actual_result: Alabama Crimson Tide 5.07 yards per pass attempt against Tennessee Volunteers 6.36.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Alabama as better in QB and the game went the other way. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: every signal this claim rests on went the other way
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 21.3 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 8 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing, defence.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.pregame_expectation: The model published an outcome range of -28.8 → +13.2 (Tennessee).
lessons.actual_result: The game finished outside it, at a margin of 16.
lessons.lesson: The published range is meant to contain eight results in ten. A miss is expected roughly twice in ten games and is only a problem in aggregate — which is exactly what this store exists to measure.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Count range misses across the season. A rate materially above 20% means the model’s stated uncertainty is too narrow.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk published a fair total of 55.
lessons.actual_result: The game finished with 36 points, an error of 19.
lessons.lesson: A total missed by this much usually means a pace or a finishing assumption was wrong, not that both ratings were. Check which of the two moved.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Was the play count or the points per drive the miss? Both are in this game’s result record.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Tennessee +7.0 where the market has Tennessee +5.5 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at FanDuel — a 1.3 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Alabama Crimson Tide lost by 16. the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.lesson: The market had the better estimate here. EdgeDesk’s disagreement was not information on this game, and the honest reading is that the price already contained what the model thought it had found.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Track disagreements of this size across the season. The question is not whether one landed; it is whether the class of them has any edge at all.
